newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: NAR retains control of Tobago assembly.
newsitem.headline: NAR retains control of Tobago assembly.

text.p: The National Alliance for Reconstruction (NAR) retained control of Tobago's House of Assembly but with a slightly reduced majority, final results from Monday's election showed.
The NAR won 10 out of 12 seats in the Caribbean island's council, the People's National Movement won one seat and independent candidate Debra Moore-Miggins, a lawyer, took the other.
In the last assembly, the NAR held 11 seats, and the PNM one. Turnout for the polls was around 40 percent, an election official said.

Under new constitutional arrangements granting more autonomy to the 116-square mile (300 sq km) sister island of Trinidad, a new chief secretary will be named from the elected assemblymen. Sources speculate that NAR candidate Hochoy Charles will be appointed to the post.
The new assembly will be inaugurated on Wednesday by Trinidad and Tobago President Noor Hassanali.

The islands of Trinidad and Tobago have been linked together since 1889 in a unitary state. But last week Tobago was granted more power by the national parliament in Port of Spain, the Trinidad capital.
